items.text: The background-drawing worker threads no longer hold 64 MB of memory for the life of the app.
The clipped collapsed sidebar rail is traced past its own window and parked for an on-screen capture.
A large picture's ~460 MB memory spike is traced to WebView2's in-process response hand-off, not the decode; the fix is split to T3241.
An agent update during a relaunch no longer leaves a window behind until the next launch.
The composited title bar, tab strip and sidebar share the panes' graphics device instead of building their own.
The ~200 MB a first burst of panes leaves behind is named: it is the NVIDIA GL driver's own arena.
Perf baseline-4: busy output wakes the app about 8x less, but idle CPU and the session agent got worse.
The agent's flood CPU is named: one message per ~113-byte ConPTY line, not parsing.
Closing viewers leaks nothing per open: the residue was a terminal tab's driver arena plus one-time WebView2 warm-up.
pane-ingest-ab scores the median of three interleaved runs per arm, and the stable verdict exposes a real agent-pane slowdown.
